chunks: From him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not permissible for her to perform khul' (divorce by redemption) until she says to her husband:
Then he mentioned what our companions mentioned,
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It was permitted for women in what is less than this.'
So when she says to her husband, 'My khul' is lawful, and it is lawful for my husband what he took from me,' and there remain two talaqs upon him, then the khul' counts as one talaq.
And the statement (of khul') must come only from her.
Then he said: 'If the matter were up to us, the divorce would not be except for the waiting period (i.e., one talaq would suffice, and khul' would not count as a separate divorce).
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on khul' and how does it affect the count of talaqs in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies the mechanics of khul' as a distinct legal instrument, emphasizing that the wife's declaration triggers the divorce and allows the husband to retain the compensation, a practice rooted in the Prophet's time. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) contrasts this established ruling with his preferred view that khul' should be absorbed into the waiting period (iddah) rather than counting as a separate talaq, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence between the operative ruling (hukm al-'amal) and the ideal ruling (hukm al-mawdu').
